newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Adtranz wins share of Turkish rail order.
newsitem.headline: Adtranz wins share of Turkish rail order.

text.p: Adtranz Sweden, which is co-owned by ABB and Daimler-Benz, said on Wednesday said it had won a half share of a 2.2 billion crown order to supply a new rapid tram system to the Turkish city of Adana.

"Of the total order value of around 2.2 billion crowns, half goes to Adtranz Sweden, which is the leader of a consortium with the construction company ALARKO and ABB Elektrik of Turkey," the company said in a statement.

It said the project covered design, contruction and installation of a rapid tram system as well as operative support in the first year. The total line length for the first phase of this project would be 13.3 kms.
ALARKO would be responsible for the contruction, including tracks, whilst ABB Elektrik would carry out local work for Adtranz, it added.
The railcars would be delivered in 1998, and the system would be operative in 1999, Adtranz said.
It said it would be responsible for arranging complete financing of the project.
